clue.text: Harbour location strike ended, according to Spooner

indicators.note: Spooner was the Oxford don famed for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the pair is said his way

parts.note: to sock is to strike and to have died is to have ended; swap the opening sounds of that pair

explanation.surface: A dock strike has finished and the harbour is getting back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: A Spoonerism swaps the first sounds of two words, so the S and D trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: The dockside is the area along a wharf, a place found in any port.

clue.text: Books after some time degenerate

indicators.note: after places the books following the period of time in the finished word

parts.note: a decade is a span of ten years
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: Reading books over a long stretch supposedly corrupts a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes someone in moral decline, which is what the adjective degenerate also means.

clue.text: Announcer withholding nothing from Corrie broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, as seed is, so the letters are strewn into a new order
withholding means keeping something back, so a letter is held out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A TV announcer keeps quiet about a Coronation Street episode being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Corrie is the nickname of Coronation Street, a long-running British TV soap. Take O out of CORRIE and rearrange CRRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: A town crier was an official who made public announcements in the street.

clue.text: Magnificent craft going over tree

indicators.note: in a down clue going over means sitting on top, so the vessel comes first

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a craft
the lime, or linden, is a tree

explanation.surface: A splendid boat sails past a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Sublime means of such grandeur or beauty that it inspires awe, close to splendid.

clue.text: One's pulled out of water holding article

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: something out of water is dry
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is hauled out of the sea clutching a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One’s pulled' looks like a swimmer being rescued; it means a thing that gets pulled. A sits inside DRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A dray is a low heavy cart drawn by horses, traditionally used by brewers to deliver barrels.

clue.text: Drake, perhaps, removing whiskey from jacket

indicators.note: removing means taking a letter away from the following word

parts.note: a wrapper is an outer covering or jacket, as on a book
Whiskey is W in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man, maybe a duck or a sea captain, takes a whiskey bottle out of his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drake' suggests the duck or Sir Francis Drake; here it is the Canadian hip-hop star.
explanation.definitionFit: Drake is a famous Canadian hip-hop artist, so he is an example of a performer of rap music.

clue.text: One checked car in place hit by driver?

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car
in golf the tee is where the ball is struck with a driver

explanation.surface: A traffic officer inspects a car parked where a motorist crashed into it.
explanation.walkthrough: The driver is a golf club, not a motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditee is a person or organisation whose accounts are examined by an auditor.

clue.text: Case of wine, fine mixture

parts.note: port is a fortified wine
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
an olio is a miscellaneous mixture or hotchpotch

explanation.surface: A case of wine turns out to be a good blend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of wine' reads as a box of bottles, but 'Case' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: High-ranking people dispatch soldiers to the north

indicators.note: in a down entry heading north means reading upwards, so the words run backwards

parts.note: to dispatch someone is to kill them
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Senior figures send troops off to the northern front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispatch' looks like sending soldiers away, but it means to kill.
explanation.definitionFit: Royals are members of a monarch's family, who stand at the top of the social order.

clue.text: One keeping documents secure beginning to concern council after insolence

indicators.note: after puts the local authority behind the cheek in the finished word
beginning to means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of concern
lip is cheeky talk
a board is a governing council

explanation.surface: A council official guards papers after rudeness from the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A clipboard is a board with a spring clip at the top that holds sheets of paper in place.

clue.text: Scoffing fish sandwiches father served up

indicators.note: a fish that sandwiches something holds it between its two halves

parts.note: the dory, or John Dory, is a sea fish

indicators.note: in a down entry served up means presented upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down fish sandwiches that Dad has dished up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffing' suggests eating greedily; here it means mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means mocking or contemptuous, which is the jeering sense of scoffing.

clue.text: American's covering competitive event

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the American name for a bowler hat
second meaning: a famous horse race, or any contest between local rivals

explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a classic flat horse race run at Epsom in England; a derby is also a match between local rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a hard round felt hat is called a derby, and the word also names a race or local sporting contest.

clue.text: Beginning to embrace divorced Royal Institute scientist

indicators.note: to embrace means to wrap around what follows
divorced means split apart, so the two letters sit separately inside rather than together

parts.note: dawn is the beginning of something
R is the abbreviation for Royal
I is the abbreviation for Institute

explanation.surface: A divorced fellow of the Royal Institution starts a new relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divorced' tells you the two abbreviations do not sit side by side but go in at different points.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Darwin was the English naturalist who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection.

clue.text: Pleased bear pinching cheese runs back

indicators.note: back means everything built so far is read in the other direction
pinching means gripping, so the carrying word closes around what follows

parts.note: to lug is to carry, or bear
feta is a Greek cheese
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A happy bear steals cheese and runs off home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal but is the verb to carry, and 'back' turns round the whole construction, not just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grateful means thankful, and someone thankful for a favour is pleased with it.

clue.text: Control playing piece, pinning one knight

indicators.note: pinning means holding something fast inside, so the playing piece grips the next item

parts.note: a domino is a playing piece
I is the Roman numeral one
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A chess player gains control by pinning a lone knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinning' sounds like the chess tactic; it puts I inside DOMINO, and N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominion means sovereignty or rule over territory or people, which is power and control.

clue.text: Assuredness backing general, manipulated soft figure to protect king

indicators.note: to protect means to shield by surrounding, so the mixed letters enclose the monarch
manipulated means handled and worked into another shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
seven is a number, or figure
R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the military man's name runs backwards

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A general's confidence is shaken by a weak character guarding the king, as in a chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' here means reversed, not supporting; 'figure' is a number spelt out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves of steel is an idiom for great composure and courage under pressure, which is assuredness.

clue.text: Cook ignores an argument

indicators.note: to cook the books is to falsify them, so cook means the letters are doctored into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef pays no attention to a quarrel in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Reasoning is the line of logic offered in support of a case, which is what an argument is.

clue.text: Compound is reopen after renovation

indicators.note: a renovated building is remade, so the letters are rebuilt in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A walled compound opens its gates again once building work is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests an enclosure; it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Isoprene is a volatile hydrocarbon used to make synthetic rubber, a chemical substance made of bonded elements.

clue.text: This writer involved in a revolutionary fuel shares advances

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside what follows

parts.note: taken as written
the setter refers to themself as me

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right round, so the next word is read backwards

parts.note: oil is a fuel
rations are allotted shares

explanation.surface: A writer is caught up in an energy revolution and sees share prices climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shares' suggests stock-market holdings; it means portions handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ameliorations are improvements, and advances in the noun sense means steps of progress.

clue.text: Top network operator impacted by strikes

indicators.note: impacted by means pressed hard into, so the strikes are driven inside the operator

parts.note: EE is a British mobile phone network
clips are blows, as in a clip round the ear

explanation.surface: A senior figure at a phone company is hit by industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective for the boss; it is the verb meaning to outdo.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse someone is to surpass or outshine them, which is the verb sense of top.

clue.text: Biting food female's left uncooked

parts.note: a tart remark is sharp or biting

indicators.note: female's left means the female has departed, so her letter goes from the word

parts.note: fare is food
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Spicy food a woman leaves behind has not been cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Biting food' suggests eating; Biting is TART, and FARE loses F.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare describes a dish of meat or fish served raw, as in steak tartare.

clue.text: Large letters turning up journalist separated

indicators.note: in a down entry turning up means flipping to read upwards, so the word goes backwards

parts.note: caps are capital letters
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper writer with a big headline arrives and keeps apart from others.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaced means set apart with gaps between, so the items are separated.

clue.text: Whizz around circulating mail for herald

parts.note: a whizz is an expert, or pro

indicators.note: circulating means moving about, so the letters are shifted into another order

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for around
taken as written

explanation.surface: A messenger whizzes around delivering post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herald' looks like a noun for the messenger; it is the verb meaning to announce.
explanation.definitionFit: To proclaim is to announce publicly, which is what heralding something means.

clue.text: Groom losing heart ended marital arrangement

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter goes from the word before

parts.note: to preen is to groom oneself
time is up when it has ended

explanation.surface: A bridegroom gets cold feet and the marriage plan is called off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a bridegroom; it is the verb. PREEN drops its middle E.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup, short for prenuptial agreement, is a contract settling property before a wedding.

clue.text: Green parrot's tail missing in indigenous species

indicators.note: missing in means absent from the following word, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a native is a species that occurs naturally in a place

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of parrot

explanation.surface: A green parrot is absent from a list of native wildlife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like the parrot's colour, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the sense of inexperienced or gullible matches naive, meaning lacking worldly wisdom.

clue.text: Listener's comparatively well-ventilated place

indicators.note: a listener judges by ear, so it is the sound of the words that matters

parts.note: airier means more open to fresh air

explanation.surface: Someone listening finds a room breezier than another.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent airier and area sound alike, since the final R is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or zone, a place in general terms.

clue.text: Crease from edges of clasp holding skirt

indicators.note: holding means those outer letters grip the next item between them
edges of means only the outermost letters of the next word are used

parts.note: the first and last letters of clasp
a skirt can be a border or edge, a rim

explanation.surface: A skirt gets creased where its fastening is held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like the garment but means an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp is to press into small folds or ridges, so a crimp is a crease.

clue.text: Make standard Scandinavian ferries land in Africa

indicators.note: a ferry carries its load inside it, so the first word holds the next

parts.note: Norse means Scandinavian
Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: Nordic ferry companies establish a regular route to an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: To normalise is to bring into line with the usual or accepted norm.

clue.text: Rank inside green bottles

indicators.note: the words bottle something up, holding it within them

parts.note: spans the end of inside and most of green

explanation.surface: Bottles of green glass contain something foul-smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank' suggests a bad smell; it means a level or grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A degree is a step on a scale of standing or status, which a rank also is.

clue.text: Recalled times eating mediocre starter in eatery? Me too!

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside, so the reversed word encloses the rest
recalled means called back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: eras are periods of time
meh is slang for mediocre

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of eatery

explanation.surface: Diners remember eating an average first course at a restaurant, and someone agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a first course; it only picks the opening letter of the word after it. Meh is a shrug of a word for so-so.
explanation.definitionFit: Same here is a colloquial reply agreeing that the speaker shares the feeling, just like me too.
